name: National Securities Depository Ltd
title: National Securities Depository Ltd - 544467 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Depository with no capacity or pricing lever: demat adds of 15.6 lakh and market share 17.2%, while costs of tech and talent keep rising and IPO-linked revenue carries the quarter; no fee hike yet.

capex.quote: 1 year before that, our capex was about INR30 crores. We elevated that to more than INR100 crores. From there on, things have sort of flattened out.

triggers.label: No issuer fee hike; settlement pricing stalled
triggers.quote: there are no progress or I would say, outcomes to report as far as price increases are concerned

triggers.label: Tech spend flattish in FY27, 'more of a build-up'
triggers.quote: this year, I think broadly it is going to be flattish compared to last year, not too much different actually

triggers.label: Retail share 17.2% vs 17.6% QoQ
triggers.quote: Market share came in at about 17.2% in Q2 FY2027 compared with 17.6% in the sequential previous quarter

triggers.label: Unlisted company onboarding saturating
triggers.quote: This year, in H1, we have onboarded about 6,500 companies

guidance.value: Not quantified; expenses to flatten from next year, timing 'very difficult to commit'
guidance.quote: we do expect operating leverage to support margin normalization as we move forward

prior_guidance_check.quote: we do expect operating leverage to support margin normalization as we move forward

red_flags.label: Consolidated EBITDA margin 30.6%; standalone PAT +5.2% vs revenue +11.6%
red_flags.quote: Our EBITDA margin on a consolidated basis for the current quarter stands at 30.6%

red_flags.label: Tech and talent cost growth well above income growth
red_flags.quote: These 3 items are growing by more than double.

evasions.topic: Expense growth and negative operating leverage
evasions.quote: you are asking some questions which are more in the domain of guidance. We really refrain from giving any guidance
we are not giving any specific guidance
But we have not quantified as of now.

summary.headline: NSDL Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 34.8% YoY to INR582.6 crores, but PAT grew only 10.9% to INR122.5 crores on elevated tech and talent costs.
summary.overview: Consolidated total income reached INR582.6 crores (+34.8% YoY), driven by a rebound in IPO and corporate-action activity, while PAT rose 10.9% YoY to INR122.5 crores. Consolidated EBITDA grew 12.5% YoY to INR178.5 crores, with margin at 30.6%, as technology and talent spending stayed elevated. Management said FY27 technology and related expenses would be broadly flat versus FY26, with growth moderating from next year, and gave no price-hike progress on issuer or settlement charges. Demat account additions were 15.6 lakh net in Q2, and NSDL's market share was 17.2% in Q2 versus 17.6% QoQ.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR106.1 crores in full FY26

segments.name: Depository (standalone core)
segments.commentary: Standalone PAT is about 88% of consolidated profit. Demat accounts reached 4.72 crore, with 320 DPs after adding about 4 in Q2 and 10 in H1. Market share was 17.2% in Q2 versus 17.6% QoQ, and 17.4% in H1 versus 16.6% in H1 FY26.

segments.name: NSDL Payments Bank
segments.commentary: Retail customers rose to 54.3 lakh from 33.5 lakh a year earlier (1.6x). Deposits grew 1.4x to INR378.1 crores. Subsidiary profit contribution is said to be above 10%, up from about 5% a year or 1.5 years earlier. Management cited UPI acquiring tie-ups as a growth driver.

segments.name: NSDL Database Management (KRA and insurance repository)
segments.commentary: KRA records reached 2.06 crore as of 30 September 2026. Cumulative dematerialised insurance policies were 1.75 crore. The insurance repository business is being transferred via a demerger application filed with NCLT Mumbai.

guidance_outlook: FY27 technology and related expenses are expected to be broadly flat versus FY26, with marginal differences possible; a specific action plan for next year is due in the next few months.
Management expects the base effect to flatten expense growth from next year, but gave no time frame for operating leverage or margin normalisation.
No guidance on market share or account additions; management said it was not giving specific guidance on retail share gains.
Settlement and issuer pricing talks with regulators remain unresolved for more than a year; no price-hike outcome to report.
capex_capacity: Technology capex rose from about INR30 crores to more than INR100 crores; spending has since flattened, per management.
Capitalised technology was INR23.9 crores in H1 FY27 versus INR106.1 crores in full FY26.
Demat 2.0 (DLT-based, tokenised bonds, CBDC settlement) is in SEBI sandbox pilot, jointly run with CDSL; 3 primary bond issuances worth a little over INR1,000 crores so far, institutional only.
Online Form 121 submission, an API-based interface with NSE for Electronic Gold Receipts, and API connectivity for bond OBPPs went live; 68+ APIs are offered to DPs.
demand_pricing: Q2 FY27 net demat additions were 15.6 lakh, against 79 lakh industry-wide additions in Q2 FY26 (about 90 lakh in Q2 FY27 industry-wide, up 14.2% YoY).
Fintech brokers were 23.5% of NSDL's incremental demat sourcing in Q2 FY27, up from 9.3% in Q2 FY26.
Run-rate market share on new accounts was about 9%, then 12%, then 14%, and is now 16-18% per management.
Unlisted issuer segment share was about 72.5%, with 3,197 companies admitted in Q2; e-voting share was about 52.4%, with 3,160 events versus 2,924 a year earlier.
IPO activity: about INR90,000 crore raised in Q2 FY27 across the primary market, including the NSE listing. Management said IPOs add roughly 25-30% to business when the pipeline is strong.
Unlisted company onboarding was about 6,500 in H1 FY27 versus about 30,000 in FY26 and 33,000 before that; management described this as saturation.
Issuer and settlement charges were unchanged; there was no IPO price increase.

qa_highlights.question: How large is the Demat 2.0 opportunity, what stage is it at, and is NSDL a first mover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described it as a SEBI-driven sandbox pilot run jointly with CDSL, with bond issuance only and no secondary market yet. Three issuances worth a little over INR1,000 crore have happened, and it is open only to institutions. Retail access depends on future SEBI evaluation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for raising retail market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called retail share gain the top priority and said the top 3 DPs hold about 60-65% of the market. About 30 new DPs were added in 1.5 years, and run-rate share has climbed from 9% to 16-18%. No specific guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will IPO and corporate action momentum continue?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Jigar Shah said YoY growth was about 24%. IPO activity adds roughly 25-30% to business when the pipeline is strong, and October saw one large IPO. Continued momentum depends on SEBI approvals.

qa_highlights.question: Will unlisted company onboarding keep falling, and how are tech expenses expected to trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said onboarding has stabilised at about 3,000 per quarter after the MCA dematerialisation rule change. Tech spend in FY27 is expected to be broadly flat versus FY26, moving from catch-up to build-up mode, with a specific action plan for next year due in coming months.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a case for an issuer pricing hike given rising costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no IPO price increase. Settlement-charge talks with regulators have been ongoing for over a year, with no outcome yet.

qa_highlights.question: Will negative operating leverage persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to commit to a time frame, citing base effects and market dependence. It said FY27 spend is largely budgeted, with future spend more discretionary, and that normalisation must come before operating leverage returns.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Payments Bank traction and MDR outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Customers are at 54 lakh, deposits at INR378 crore, and UPI acquiring tie-ups are growing. The MDR on UPI is paused, and its impact on the Payments Bank has not been quantified.

risks_watch: Consolidated PAT growth (10.9%) lags revenue growth (34.8%), so cost growth on technology, talent and depreciation is outpacing income.
Retail market share remains about 17%, and the top 3 DPs control about 60-65% of the market.
Unlisted company onboarding is saturating, which reduces a recurring revenue stream.
Issuer and settlement charge pricing is unresolved, with no timeline for regulatory action.
Dependence on IPO and corporate-action cycles; management says IPOs add 25-30% when the pipeline is strong.
Payments Bank profitability depends on UPI acquiring and on MDR regulation, which is currently paused.
summary.management_tone: Confident on franchise growth, Demat 2.0 and Payments Bank traction, but cautious and non-committal on costs and pricing. Management repeatedly declined to give guidance on expense normalisation, market share and timing of operating leverage.
key_quotes: So one has to look at technology investments as a medium-term business enabler really rather than just an expense, and that's how we see it.
There are no progress or I would say, outcomes to report as far as price increases are concerned.
So it is not as if we are, in a sense, got early mover, but we have moved together.
Before negative operating leverage starts kicking in, you need to show normalization of expenses and then operating leverage comes in.

adds.what: Demat 2.0 DLT-based tokenised bond and CBDC settlement pilot (SEBI sandbox, jointly with CDSL); not productive capacity

growth.why: No numeric revenue guidance; management said FY27 tech spend will be broadly flat versus FY26 and expense growth should flatten from next year with operating leverage timing not committed, while demat share fell to 17.2% and price-hike talks remain unresolved, so the outlook is flat to unclear.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consolidated EBITDA margin at 30.6% and EBITDA up only 12.5% vs total income up 34.8%, but management gave no timeframe and said FY27 tech spend is broadly flat vs FY26, so operating leverage depends on expense flattening from next year and market activity.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No physical capacity or plant expansion discussed; tech capitalisation fell to INR23.9 crores in H1 FY27 from INR106.1 crores in full FY26 and spend has flattened, so no new capacity is signalled.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Net demat additions were 15.6 lakh in Q2 vs 79 lakh industry-wide in Q2 FY26, NSDL's share slipped to 17.2% from 17.6% QoQ, and IPO activity (about INR90,000 crore raised in Q2) adds 25-30% to business when the pipeline is strong, but the unlisted onboarding base is saturating at about 3,000 per quarter.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Technology capex has flattened after rising from about INR30 crores to over INR100 crores, and utilisation is not a relevant metric for this depository; no new capex was announced.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no numeric guidance and declined to commit on market share, account additions or operating leverage timing, with the outlook described as flat to unclear.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: PAT growth of 10.9% lags income growth of 34.8%, FY27 tech spend is budgeted flat, and issuer and settlement price-hike talks are unresolved for over a year, leaving no pricing cushion if IPO activity slows.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Demat 2.0 (DLT-based tokenised bonds and CBDC settlement) is in a SEBI sandbox with 3 bond issuances worth a little over INR1,000 crores, institutional only, and retail access depends on future SEBI evaluation; not yet commercial.

rows.label: Payments Bank UPI acquiring and customer growth
rows.why: Retail customers reached 54.3 lakh (1.6x YoY) and deposits INR378.1 crores (1.4x), with the subsidiary's profit contribution above 10% and UPI acquiring tie-ups cited as the growth driver, though MDR is paused and its impact is unquantified.

rows.label: Insurance repository demerger to NCLT
rows.why: A demerger application for the insurance repository business has been filed with NCLT Mumbai, with 1.75 crore cumulative dematerialised policies, but no approval timeline was given.

rows.label: Issuer and settlement charge hike
rows.why: Settlement and issuer pricing talks with regulators have been unresolved for more than a year, with no IPO price increase and no timeline for regulatory action.

tone.note: Management was confident on the franchise, Demat 2.0 and Payments Bank traction, but cautious and non-committal on tech and talent costs, pricing and operating leverage timing; analysts pressed on margin normalisation, market share and the IPO cycle.
